description:
Team Vitala is a two-member team formed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, bringing together scientific curiosity, technical development, and a shared interest in making complex ideas understandable and accessible. The project combines biological reasoning, software development, and thoughtful science communication.

Our guiding principle: Build with curiosity. Question with science. Design with purpose.
summary:
AETHER is an offline-first astronaut investigation and mission-support prototype designed for long duration spaceflight, where reliable connectivity and immediate-medical support cannot be assumed. 
The application brings together sleep, heart-rate, activity and self-reported fatigue observations through manual entry and local JSON/CSV imports. Rather than issuing unverified diagnosis, AETHER examines measurement quality, individual baselines, trends and operational contexts to distinguishing observations requiring review from missing or uncertain evidence.
Six fictional crew workspaces provide personalized records, meanwhile a structured investigation workflow connects findings with follow-up actions, re-assessments and upcoming mission activites. The system supports local record storage, optional profile encryption and exportable crew handovers. Its radiation component demonstrates uncalibrated count-rate analysis without claiming medical-dose estimates.
Informed by NASA Human Research resources, AETHER explores the transparency of human-in-the-loop software can help astronauts understand health observations and prepare for mission activites without relying on continuous connectivity.
details:
AETHER: Health observations to mission-aware decisions.

The problem

The space missions are of a long duration and pose a challenge to the traditional healthcare workflows. Sleep disturbance, changes in physical activity, cardiovascular responses, exposure to radiation, and operational fatigue can all affect astronauts, as well as cause delays in communication and in having immediate access to support on Earth.

Once measurements are taken, it is not enough to have an onboard monitoring system. Crews also should know if the observation is dependable, what factors may account for the observation, and what information and follow-up is required prior to a subsequent activity.

Our solution

AETHER is an offline-first astronaut health investigation and mission-support prototype that follows a four-stage process:

Observe → Interpret in Context → Identify Follow-Up → Reassess

The app includes four main parameters: sleep time, heart rate, activity and subjective fatigue.

Entry of measurements can be made by hand or imported from locally stored CSV/JSON files. Before observations are added to the investigation workflow a validation pipeline performs checks on formats, units, missing values, duplicate records and measurement provenance.

Scientific uncertainty and reasoning.

AETHER does not rely on a generative medical chatbot, instead, it is based on a deterministic, explainable TypeScript investigation engine. It considers the quality of measurement, individual baselines, trends, and contextual information such as the circumstances of a measurement in its demonstration rules.

The software clearly separates the observations that are subject to review, the observations where there is no specific concern and the cases where there is no evidence or evidence is not sufficient under the demonstrations rules.

It maintains measurement gaps without adding simulated measurements and it keeps simulated data separate from user entered and imported data.

NASA human research resources provide guidance to the project on key spaceflight health issues and the need to monitor, contextualize, and practice operation caution.

Crew Workspace and Mission Support.

Six fictional astronaut profiles illustrate personalized health baselines, individual health records, and varied operational roles.

The application brings health investigations into an upcoming mission activity timeline, health follow-up logging and exportable crew review documentation.

The aim is to create an interactive visual companion to the crew, so that users can use these existing workflows, without creating medical diagnoses and without replacing the scientific investigation engine.

Offline architecture and implementation

AETHER is developed using React, TypeScript and a progressive web application architecture with locally-cached application assets to facilitate Vite.

It includes browser-based local persistence, optional passphrase encrypted profile, client side measurement processing and JSON/Markdown handover exports.

During normal usage, the application needs no cloud-hosted generative AI service. There is no claim of hardware telemetry acquisition, external measurements are acquired via local file import at the moment.

Radiation analysis

A dedicated experimental radiation element provides calculations of count-rates from raw detector counts and collection time.

The absorbed dose, the effective dose and validated biological risk are not reported for uncalibrated counts per second. The software deliberately avoids unsupported dosimetry conversions.

Innovation and purpose or impact.

The key aspect of AETHER's contribution is the link between the integrity of measurements, an explainable situation-specific investigation, a meaningful follow-up, and future mission activities.

The prototype is not intended to present data without any interpretation or without making any clinical predictions, but to explore how health observations can be organized by the astronaut and how they can be prepared for human decisions in a connectivity constrained environment.

Limitations

AETHER is a research and demonstration prototype, not a medical device or spaceflight system of operation.

The characters in its astronauts section and the measurements it demonstrates are made up. It does not have validated flight-medicine thresholds for its decision rules. The application is not used to make any diagnoses, prescribe treatment or authorise mission activities by itself.

Representative sensor data and expert evaluation in the domain, calibrated measuring devices, operational usability evaluation and formal medical supervision are required for future validation.

Development and verification

It was done with React, TypeScript, Vite, and browser storage and cryptography APIs along with some open source libraries. AI tools aided in software implementation, iteration, and development support; the team is responsible for scientific decisions and decisions regarding scientific review, testing, attribution, and submission accuracy.

Importation from local and investigation changes, crew-profile isolation, persistence, offline behavior, and exports are some of the key workflows that have been exercised via automated tests and browser-based evaluation. The identified defects during the review are being addressed prior to final release.
